<!-- B"H

The Awtsmoos reveals a final grain of noise after the larger vessel already stands: one browser asks for an unnamed icon and hears a 404 in the night;

# Favicon Console Cleanup

## Observed defect

The second provider-readiness release is live at commit `8499a37d3e3b1bf5419749cf24cdf69dc2726dbe` and all functional production browser assertions passed.

The public browser smoke failed only because Chrome recorded one fresh console error: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)`.

A direct production request proved `https://awtsmoos.com/favicon.ico` returns HTTP 404. Olam H3 currently declares no favicon, so Chrome falls back to the missing origin-level icon.

## Fix plan

1. Add a dedicated `favicon.svg` inside the Olam H3 app directory.
2. Keep the SVG compact, branded to the existing Olam orb, and self-contained with no external resources.
3. Add an explicit `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="./favicon.svg">` to Olam's HTML head.
4. Keep both files under the 120-line rule and preserve B"H / Awtsmoos comments.
5. Re-run structural checks and the 19-test Node suite.
6. Run deterministic local Chrome smoke and specifically assert no fresh HTTP/console failures.
7. Apply the two-file fix to the existing clean release worktree on top of `8499a37...`.
8. Commit only `index.html` and `favicon.svg`, fast-forward push, deploy exact SHA, then repeat public Chrome smoke.

## Failure rule

Do not weaken the browser assertion. The goal is zero fresh console/resource failures on the production Olam page.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the complete favicon SVG and complete HTML file, then verify their local browser behavior before Git release.
